miniProject.title: Workload arithmetic and a falsifiable claim record for kernellab
miniProject.brief: Start the one repository the whole track builds on. Create kernellab with harness/, kernels/cuda/, kernels/triton/, refs/, tests/, profiles/, reports/ and manifests/, then fix one transformer workload, derive its operations and bytes, sweep one batched matmul from floor to plateau, and file a claim record with a prediction and a falsifier before any later kernel is timed. The harness, the manifests and the sweep carry into every later section.
steps: Create kernellab with harness/, kernels/cuda/, kernels/triton/, refs/, tests/, profiles/, reports/ and manifests/ directories. Write `manifests/env.json` with GPU name, driver, toolkit, PyTorch and CUDA versions, `nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK` output and the SM clock observed during timing, plus the code revision. Every later run appends its raw trials to reports/ with the revision that produced them, so any number traces back to code, workload and hardware.

Fix one workload card with medians, spread and an arrival note: prompt length, output length, batch, dtype and shape medians plus whether arrivals are closed loop or Poisson. Include the worked card with \(P = 4096\), \(G = 1024\) and \(B = 16\): sequences finishing per step 1/64 and tokens evicted per step 80. State which cold trials are discarded (first compile, first weight load, first autotune) before the warm median is read.

Sweep bf16 `[B, 4096] x [4096, 4096]` matmuls on the desktop RTX 3050 6 GB with CUDA events, warmup and interleaved repeats, plus a device-to-device copy at the same sizes. Plot achieved TFLOP/s against \(B\) and report the knee and the small-batch floor. On the reference card with PyTorch 2.14.1 every \(B\) from 1 to 16 took 0.24 to 0.29 ms, throughput was 6.5 TFLOP/s at \(B = 64\), 13.4 at 128, 14.2 at 256, 14.8 at 1024 and 16.0 at 4096, and the copy reached 151.4 GB/s for a plateau ratio near 95 with the knee between 64 and 128. Your numbers will differ; the target is a knee near your own measured peak-over-bandwidth ratio, with raw samples kept.

Derive the workload arithmetic closed-book for the invented 18.4e9 parameter model: dense decode work \(2 \times 18.4 \times 10^9 = 3.68 \times 10^{10}\) operations per token, attention \(4 \times 8192 \times 32 \times 256 \times 64 = 1.72 \times 10^{10}\) at cached length 8192 for a total near \(5.4 \times 10^{10}\), int8 key-value bytes per token 262144, and the 13B bf16 cache at 8192 context near \(6.7 \times 10^9\) bytes with the 81920 byte per token GQA int8 variant. Time the sweep from the previous step against these counts and name the bound on each side of the ridge.

Implement Etalon Algorithm 1 in refs/ and score the two Section 4 traces at 100 ms deadline: both take one TBT miss in 11 while fluidity-index gives 1.0 to the 10 ms system and 10/11 to the 100 ms system. Apply it to one real timestamp trace with a fitted prefill deadline, then bound attention work at 31 percent share (at most 1.45x end to end) and intermediates at 10 percent (at most 1.11x) with the formula \(S = 1/(1-f+f/r)\), and reconcile the 1-GPU FasterTransformer case as \(16.8/0.9\) near 18.7 ms plus 2.2 ms of intermediates near 20.9 ms against 22.0 measured.

File one claim record in manifests/ before profiling: workload, hardware, baseline, timing boundary, correctness method, prediction and the falsifying signal that would reject it. Name a strong baseline at matched workload (library, compiler or engine, with precision and flags), keep an independent reference that shares no logic with the timed path, and consume and check outputs before any speed claim. Add the training-step check as a derived extra: \(6 \times 3 \times 10^6 \times 13 \times 10^9\) operations near 310 ms at the stated peak share, with the comms-bound verdict for pure FSDP stated as a prediction.
deliverables: kernellab with harness/, kernels/cuda/, kernels/triton/, refs/, tests/, profiles/, reports/ and manifests/, the environment manifest and the workload card with medians, spread and arrival note.
The bf16 batch sweep with raw interleaved trials, the copy result, the knee and floor, and the ridge calculation from measured peak over measured bandwidth.
The closed-book arithmetic sheet, the Algorithm 1 scores 1.0 and 10/11, the Amdahl bounds and the 1-GPU reconciliation with named residuals.
One filed claim record with prediction, falsifier, baseline, boundary and lineage from revision to number.

rubric.pass: The sheet derives dense, attention and byte counts against independent references, and every timed number traces to a manifest, a workload card and raw trials.
rubric.strong: Each residual names an independent line (profiled bandwidth, counted passes, timed comms) and leaves unexplained remainder unexplained.

rubric.pass: Cold trials are discarded by rule, warm medians come from interleaved repeats with raw samples kept, and the knee is compared with the measured ratio.
rubric.strong: The report shows a rotating-buffer repeat and states which cache state each run preserves.

rubric.pass: Algorithm 1 returns 1.0 and 10/11 on the toy pair, Amdahl bounds are derived before profiling, and the strong baseline is matched in workload, precision and flags.
rubric.strong: The write-up shows a case where peak throughput ranks two systems differently from the SLO qualified rate.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone laboratory: the harness, manifests, workload card, sweep and claim record are its foundation. Later sections add kernels, counters, timelines and integrations inside the same kernellab layout.
